caption:
10.1 s S windows and equal pre-P noise; three-component power sums; same UTC sample grid and dated instrument responses.
Response removed to acceleration before conversion to displacement-equivalent ASD. No amplitude matching or source/path correction.

Same stations, response epochs, processing and 10.1 s windows. Dashed lines show measured pre-P noise.
Weak-event usability changes with frequency and station; a large peak or a high coherence alone does not establish a resolved source plateau.

80 s full-wave windows and equal pre-P noise; NW=2, K=3. Shading marks 0.05–0.2 Hz.
The lowest frequency has four cycles per window. These spectra assess relative sensor performance; they are not new moment-tensor inversions.

Ratios use noise-subtracted three-component power where both amplitude SNRs ≥3; missing curves indicate insufficient shared SNR.
Coherence is a power-weighted mean of matching component coherences. Shading marks 0.7–1.2 Hz; no fitted gain or polarity changes are applied.

The control uses 100 sps and a known displacement amplitude. The right panel is computed directly from each full instrument response.
A 60 dB floor is relative to the largest displacement-response gain. Its frequency dependence differs for velocity and acceleration sensors.
This demonstrates a processing effect; it does not by itself quantify the bias of any previously fitted earthquake magnitude.

0.7–3 Hz zero-phase filter after response correction; same UTC grid and physical amplitude units, with no fitted rescaling.
CHJ3 closely agrees. BURB has an amplitude discrepancy; HANB’s horizontal phase differences warrant an orientation check.
